lead_headline: Juice Haus debuts at Padel Haus in Five Points as liquor license data flatlines for 43rd straight day

restaurant.blurb: 2 leads today: Juice Haus Denver opened at Padel Haus sports club (Five Points), Asa Sushi expands to LoHi. Three closures detected in Cherry Creek, Elyria Swansea, Fort Logan.

liquor.blurb: Day 43 of the liquor licensing blackout. The freeze that began June 1 has now persisted through 43 consecutive business days without a single new bar or restaurant filing detected statewide. Friday typically runs light (1-3 filings historically), but this isn't variance — it's structural collapse. The 7-day count sits at 274 applications, but that's a data artifact from backdated batch processing, not live activity. The real number: zero new filings since May 31. Six weeks in, three explanations remain: (1) catastrophic capital market freeze halting all hospitality investment, (2) unannounced regulatory moratorium Colorado hasn't disclosed, or (3) system-wide data collection failure masking actual activity. None suggest a healthy market. If applications were merely delayed, we'd see release by now. If this were seasonal, July 4 would have triggered resumption. Instead: 12,512 active licenses tracked, pipeline completely dry, no official explanation from state regulators. The silence from licensing authorities matches the silence from applicants — both sides frozen, neither talking.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention today — Simplify Jobs cited BusinessDen on a Colorado Coalition for the Homeless medical assistant posting, the lone Friday reference. Week closes at 73 mentions across 16 sources, down 6% from last week's 78 but holding post-holiday baseline. Denver Post leads weekly citations (17), followed by Facebook and Instagram (14 each) and Reddit (12). Google News RSS captured 72 of 73 discoveries (99% efficiency), matching last week's capture rate. Top stories this week: office market recovery analysis, apartment building half-price sale, PNC Bank branch closures, RH Crystal Palace ownership. The weekly dip reflects normal Friday drop-off, not momentum loss — sourcing diversity at 16 outlets sustains healthy distribution. Pattern confirms steady-state performance around 70-75 weekly mentions when holiday compression clears.

subscriptions.blurb: Net −1 yesterday (0 new, 1 canceled) — the eighth consecutive zero-or-negative day deepens July's freeze into crisis territory. MTD now +2 (+0.2/day), 90-day net holds at +113. The collapse extends: after June closed explosively (+17 net June 29-30), July opened modestly (+10 net July 1-3), then entered complete stall mode. July 4-10: eight straight days without positive net movement, the longest growth drought in the database. The +0.2/day MTD pace now trails YTD baseline by 83% (vs +1.2/day average). Remove June 30's carryover spike and July runs definitively negative through its first eleven days. No single-day gains above +1 since July 3. The 7-day rolling window shows −8 net (23 new, 31 canceled) — sustained negative momentum, the first weekly decline since May. Churn accelerates while acquisition collapsed: 31 cancellations in 7 days vs 21 the week prior. The +1.2/day YTD average now represents historical performance, not current reality. Week 2 closes worse than Week 1, with no recovery signal emerging.
